races.name: Rod Gaskin Garden Machinery Handicap

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely tactical pace, solid Thirsk third off this mark last week shows current form
runners_data.spotlight: Good third off this mark at Thirsk (6f, good) last week, doing best of those drawn in single figures and that despite meeting some trouble in running; has plenty of form on soft in France; one to take seriously.

runners_data.name: Mister Bluebird
runners_data.note: Non-runner removes the only natural front-runner, creating pace vacuum that changes race dynamics completely
runners_data.comment: 8yo who has been as good as ever this spring, runner-up on last two starts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: 10lb higher than when making all in the corresponding race 12 months ago; two runner-up finishes over 7f, one of them here, this spring; weakened into midfield over 7f at Epsom on Friday; will need a career best to win this race for a second time.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who handles soft ground well, quick turnaround from yesterday's Epsom run could be positive or negative
runners_data.comment: Ideally needs soft/heavy; favourably treated off 4lb below last winning mark
runners_data.spotlight: Sprinter who is happiest on slow ground and gave some encouragement returned to 6f on soft at Epsom yesterday, where he finished mid-division having been squeezed out at the start; 4lb lower than for his last win.

runners_data.name: Brosay
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with soft ground preference, weight drop and return to favoured conditions after moderate season
runners_data.spotlight: Won 6f handicaps at Windsor and Ascot last summer; dropped down the weights in defeat this season but there have been glimmers of promise and ground softer than good will be of benefit; ran no sort of race at Carlisle eight days ago (in cheekpieces) but his usual blinkers are back on today; Oisin Murphy booked; interesting.

runners_data.name: Seven Questions
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to contest early lead in pace vacuum, 3lb penalty for recent Goodwood win to overcome
runners_data.spotlight: Ended a two-year barren spell when getting up late in a 5f handicap here 16 days; 3lb higher mark to deal with but he has a Group 3 win on his record and conditions won't faze him; respected.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Better on AW but prominent style gives tactical advantage, good third at Windsor suggests turf form improving
runners_data.comment: Possibly best to forgive last two efforts; still well treated on AW form
runners_data.spotlight: Better on AW than turf but handicapped accordingly and he ran his best race on grass when third of seven at Windsor 13 days ago (good to firm); down the field in two runs on soft but his Ayr Silver Cup effort wasn't too bad; new cheekpieces could give him a lift.

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 24-day break, strong AW form last autumn but limited recent turf evidence
runners_data.comment: Returned to form when 2nd of six at Bath but may prove vulnerable in this hotter contest
runners_data.spotlight: Did well for new yard last autumn, winning three times (5f, AW/good to soft), and he has run some solid races in defeat in 2026; this will be just his third run at 6f and others bring more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Jungle Drums
runners_data.note: Prominent style but 70-day layoff is significant concern, generally struggled for current yard except one AW win
runners_data.spotlight: Generally struggled for this yard but the notable exception came when dead-heating at Chelmsford last October (6f, AW); beaten 19l at Doncaster on his return ten weeks ago; not a solid option.

runners_data.name: Fleetwater
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with 62-day break, consistent place record this year but vulnerable returning from extended absence
runners_data.comment: Wasn't disgraced in a stronger race over C&D nine days ago; considered down in grade
runners_data.spotlight: Both wins at Windsor but she is effective elsewhere; runner-up in two of her three starts this year but she's back from nine weeks off and could prove vulnerable.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Bluebird (non-runner) was the only confirmed front-runner, leaving Seven Questions, Sudden Flight, Sturlasson and Jungle Drums to battle for prominent positions in a pace vacuum. This creates a scrappy early gallop with multiple horses wanting the same real estate, likely producing stop-start fractions through the first 3f. The lack of a natural pacesetter means the tempo will be modest early before quickening significantly from 2f out as the prominent quartet jostle for position. This messy, tactical affair strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early congestion and finish fastest when the race opens up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes tactical with multiple horses fighting for prominence
scenarios.body: The prominent runners compromise each other through uneven fractions and positioning battles, allowing the back-markers clean runs to sweep past in the final furlong. Toyotomi, Solar Aclaim, Brosay and Fleetwater all benefit from staying out of trouble and having fewer pace questions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners (likely Seven Questions) establishes a clear lead by halfway
scenarios.body: Seven Questions or Sudden Flight gets first run on their rivals and the hold-up horses are left with too much to do on the testing ground. The winner comes from those who positioned themselves handily rather than getting buried in the pack.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a 1f dash
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure speed test in the final furlong where class and recent form matter less than raw pace. Fleetwater's fresher legs or Brosay's old ability could surface in a blanket finish where margins are minimal.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet go too fast trying to establish position
scenarios.body: Seven Questions, Sudden Flight, Sturlasson and Jungle Drums all empty out from 2f home after an unsustainable battle, leaving a massive gap for the hold-up horses to close. Only the strongest finishers can bridge the gap effectively.

watchPoints.text: Seven Questions and Sudden Flight clash early for the lead position as both want to be prominent in the pace vacuum
Toyotomi gets shuffled back too far given the likelihood of a sprint finish on testing ground
Solar Aclaim shows effects of quick turnaround after yesterday's Epsom effort in the closing stages
Jungle Drums travels well early despite the long layoff, suggesting fitness levels are adequate
The pace through the first two furlongs is too strong as four horses fight for prominence

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Bulletsnap
runners_data.comment: Yard in great form so must be considered on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 85,000euros foal; second foal; by Minzaal; dam French Listed-placed 7.5f-8.5f winner (including 2yo/AW; RPR 93), sister to useful French 1m-1m4f winner Anobe; betting should be revealing for a stable in fine form.

runners_data.name: The Harv
runners_data.spotlight: 65,000euros yearling, £260,000 breeze-up 2yo; second foal; half-brother to Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner Awraad (RPR 78); dam 5f/6f winner (including 2yo/AW; 88); Irish trainer saddled a winning 2yo newcomer on Wednesday; Oisin Murphy booked; of obvious interest.

runners_data.name: Mobadir
runners_data.comment: Early February foal by No Nay Never; the oldest runner in the field; respected yard
runners_data.spotlight: Left trailing over 1f out on his Salisbury debut (5f, good) 24 days ago, dropping out to finish last of the six runners (Oakford a neck and one position ahead in fifth); can do better and 6f should suit.

runners_data.name: Asgar
runners_data.comment: Early foal; stable often gets them ready first time; makes plenty of appeal on pedigree
runners_data.spotlight: Smart pedigree but in need of the experience when down the field in a 6f maiden at Newbury last month (good ground; 12-1); this looks less demanding and he is open to improvement.

runners_data.name: My A'Ali Baba
runners_data.comment: March foal; 32,000gns yearling, £23,000 breeze-up 2yo; market likely to be a fair guide
runners_data.spotlight: Looked an unlikely winner for the first 4.5f of his Chepstow debut (6f, good to soft) but the penny dropped in the closing stages and he ultimately ran out a decisive winner; the bare form is nothing special and he will need more to defy a penalty but he is open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Oakford
runners_data.spotlight: In need of the experience when fifth of six at Salisbury (5f, good) 24 days ago, finishing a neck in front of the reopposing Mobadir; open to improvement over this extra furlong.

races.name: Goodwood Horseracing Club Membership Selling Stakes

runners_data.name: Cavan Lady
runners_data.note: Lightly raced newcomer with unknown pace style but breeding suggests speed, making debut in sellers concerning despite decent pedigree
runners_data.spotlight: 25,000gns yearling; fourth foal; half-sister to winners Nibras Angel (7f; RPR 96) and Doha Bu Thaila (Qatari 6.5f-10.5f); dam 7f/1m winner (78), sister to 5f-7f winner Munfarrid, half-sister to Listed-placed 6.5f 2yo/1m winner Morning Post; useful pedigree for one starting out in selling company; betting to guide.

runners_data.name: Beach Ahead
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who needs pace to aim at, showed promise on debut at Windsor but quick drop to sellers suggests limitations
runners_data.spotlight: Never a threat but it was still a promising start to his career when fourth of 12 in a 6f maiden at Windsor two weeks ago (good to firm); quickly drops into selling company and he is open to improvement but others have achieved more.

runners_data.name: Leucothea
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with Oisin Murphy booked, handles soft ground and has tactical speed to control this small field
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten favourite in maidens at Bath (5.7f, firm) and Wolverhampton (6f, AW) but she hasn't run badly on either occasion; has the speed to cope with 5f and Oisin Murphy booked now she drops into selling company.

runners_data.name: Fortunate
runners_data.note: Prominent racer showing recent improvement, suited by the step down in class after competitive Chester seller effort
runners_data.comment: Poor form in her three starts and she looked a hard ride latest; easy enough to swerve
runners_data.spotlight: Poor form on her first three starts but she showed much more when fourth of 12 in a Chester seller (6f, good) eight days ago, prominent throughout and only losing second in the closing stages; now has something to build on and can go well back at 5f.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with consistent form, needs strong pace but soft ground may hinder his finishing kick from rear
runners_data.comment: Leading form claims now dropping into a seller; draw not ideal but can't discount
runners_data.spotlight: Promise in all four starts, keeping on for second in a 6f seller at Chester eight days ago (passed the reopposing Fortunate, who was better drawn, close home); untried on slower than good; leading form claims.

races.paceDynamic: Leucothea will take this field along from the front with no obvious pace pressure in this small field. The confirmed leader has shown she can sustain her speed over 6f, so she should dictate comfortable fractions early before the field closes up in the final 2f. With Beach Ahead and Undercover Affair both hold-up horses needing to come from behind, and only Fortunate likely to race prominently, this sets up perfectly for the front-runner to control proceedings. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and the pace-setter, as the soft ground will make it difficult for hold-up horses to quicken decisively from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leucothea Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Leucothea breaks cleanly and dictates uncontested fractions
scenarios.body: She can sustain her gallop on the testing ground while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground from behind. Murphy can judge the pace perfectly and kick clear when the closers are still struggling through the soft turf.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Fortunate Presses Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Fortunate tracks Leucothea closely and applies early pressure
scenarios.body: The pace becomes more honest which could set things up for a late closer to strike, but Fortunate's recent improvement suggests she can battle on. Both prominent runners could tire late on the soft ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Levels Field
scenarios.trigger: If the testing conditions negate pace advantages and favour stamina
scenarios.body: The race becomes a slog where class and stamina matter more than position, potentially suiting the higher-rated newcomer or experienced campaigners. Late pace becomes crucial as early speed counts for less.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Beach Ahead Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the newcomer Beach Ahead shows significant improvement from debut
scenarios.body: His hold-up style could work if the pace collapses completely and he has more ability than his maiden fourth suggested. The Moores' yard form and quick turnaround to sellers could indicate confidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Leucothea breaks slowly or gets pressured early, as she needs to establish her lead to control the race
Monitor how quickly Undercover Affair and Beach Ahead can get into contention on the soft ground from their rear positions
Check if Fortunate can stay close enough to Leucothea without over-racing, as her best form comes when prominent
Observe Cavan Lady's early positioning as her pace style is unknown and could impact the race dynamic
Watch for any market moves on Beach Ahead given his quick reappearance and drop to selling company

races.name: Weatherbys/British EBF Agnes Keyser Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Botagoz
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with strong Listed form at York, 23 days since last run gives her freshness edge on testing ground
runners_data.spotlight: Won novice events on first two starts, latterly at Nottingham (1m, good) in April; good third of seven in Listed race at York (1m, good) last month, with major late gains from out the back to suggest this longer trip will prompt further improvement; it is needed but she is one to consider.

runners_data.name: Rose Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with Group entries, excellent soft going record (2 from 3) and 35-day break aids fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Has Group 1 entries in Coronation Stakes (1m) and Irish Oaks (1m4f); won newcomers' event at Deauville (7f, soft) last August and a rallying fourth in the Group 2 May Hill at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on her only other race as 2yo; never-dangerous tenth of 19 at 50-1 in the 1,000 Guineas at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) on reappearance but she stuck to her task, beaten about 6l, and should stay 1m2f; a leading contender, including on form.

runners_data.name: Sacred Ground
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner proven on testing ground, Gosden stable in form but needs to improve on recent Listed seconds
runners_data.comment: 2nd in two Newmarket Listed races; better form claims than most and still some potential
runners_data.spotlight: Probably acts on good to soft; won debut and runner-up in Listed events on all three starts since; this season's were over 1m2f at Newmarket (good to firm) and Newbury (good) and the latest form makes her one of the top two in this field on ratings; should be bang there again.

runners_data.name: Light Of Paris
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won easily at Newmarket, expensive breeding suggests stamina for 1m2f step-up
runners_data.spotlight: 500,000gns yearling by Sea The Stars; made a low-key debut on Kempton AW (1m3f, AW) in April but always prominent when winning a steadily run, seven-runner maiden at Ascot (1m2f, good) one month ago in tidy fashion; should improve again but this demands much better even though the second and fifth won maidens next time.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Prominent type who lacks a win from four starts, likely needs career-best to trouble these Listed performers
runners_data.comment: Form stacks up well; appears to have a workable opening mark; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Quiet improver though her four starts have not yielded a win; 1m handicap second off a mark of 80 last time (good to soft) gave hope for 1m2f but surely she has too much to find at this level.

runners_data.name: Plaid
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer improving with each run, unproven on softer than good ground creates uncertainty
runners_data.comment: Improving filly; second in Kempton handicap in March; big shout nudged up 1lb
runners_data.spotlight: Has improved a chunk with each of her four runs, last time winning off a handicap mark of 75 at Hamilton (good; unraced on softer) on the step up from 1m to 1m1f; as that win was easily by 8l, she has put herself into serious each-way calculations at this much higher level.

runners_data.name: Venetia
runners_data.note: Front-runner with course experience, headgear addition suggests connections expect improved performance
runners_data.comment: Made all at Ascot on handicap/seasonal debut and looks the type to progress further
runners_data.spotlight: Made all at Ascot (1m2f, good to firm) on handicap/seasonal debut and set steady pace when second here (1m4f, good; unraced on softer) 16 days ago; steady improver but needs a big step forward in today's first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Ourbren
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with good soft record (1 from 8), quick turnaround from 7 days ago may impact sharpness
runners_data.spotlight: Pretty useful form in Listed races on last two starts as 2yo and she duly won a Bath maiden this April; never-dangerous sixth of ten in Group 2 German 1,000 Guineas (1m, soft) latest is her best form and this new trip is not out of the question, but others have accomplished more and/or shown more potential.

runners_data.name: Della Pace
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed promise in Listed race here 15 days ago despite slow start
runners_data.comment: Ran well in AW handicap on reappearance; this is a much stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: 2yo maiden winner whose best form (from six races) came when fourth of eight in a C&D Listed race (good) two weeks ago; slowly away at 40-1 that day and made late progress, so still looks capable of a bit better; that could still mean minor honours, though.

runners_data.name: Lady Dora Mae
runners_data.note: Prominent runner unproven on soft ground, Jack Callan cannot claim in this company
runners_data.comment: Progressing and likeably consistent; dug deep to finish the job off at Windsor (1m)
runners_data.spotlight: Not proven on softer than good; ridden by Jack Callan (who can't claim in this race) on last four outings; won three of her eight races, including over 1m at Windsor on penultimate start, and best form when upped to 1m2f for second at Nottingham on latest; that handicap form, however, leaves her with major work to do.

races.paceDynamic: Venetia will make the running as the sole confirmed front-runner, with Light Of Paris and Capichera likely to track her in the early stages. The soft ground and 1m2f trip suggests Venetia can dictate a steady, sustainable gallop without pressure, particularly given her recent course experience over 1m4f here. This tactical setup creates a race where hold-up horses like Botagoz, Rose Ghaiyyath and Sacred Ground can get cover and time their challenges, while prominent racers may find themselves having to commit earlier than ideal. The pace scenario strongly favours hold-up performers who can use the testing ground and steady tempo to deliver late finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominant
scenarios.trigger: If Venetia sets a steady tempo without early pressure from prominent runners
scenarios.body: The soft ground amplifies stamina demands while reducing sprint acceleration, allowing late-running types to close decisively in the final two furlongs. Botagoz and Rose Ghaiyyath can use their proven class to time perfect challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pressure Cooker
scenarios.trigger: If Light Of Paris and Capichera press Venetia early, creating stronger fractions
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and favours horses with tactical speed who can position handily without over-racing. Light Of Paris benefits from her prominent style while Sacred Ground can track the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Venetia gets loose on the lead with soft fractions and kicks clear turning in
scenarios.body: Her course experience and recent form here gives her the tactical edge to control the race from flag to finish. The testing ground saps the finishing kick from hold-up horses who give her too much rope.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and it becomes a sprint from the 3f pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes more about raw acceleration than stamina, potentially suiting horses with higher cruise speed regardless of running style. Lady Dora Mae's recent form and Della Pace's Listed experience become more relevant.

watchPoints.text: Venetia could get loose on the lead if Light Of Paris and Capichera fail to track her early positioning
Rose Ghaiyyath may need the run after 35-day absence despite her trainer's solid recent strike-rate
Sacred Ground has been second in her last two Listed starts and needs to find extra to break that pattern
Plaid is completely unproven on ground softer than good which creates significant form doubt
Botagoz drops back to 1m2f from York's 1m but her hold-up style suits the likely steady pace scenario

races.name: Billy Vigar Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Across Earth
runners_data.note: Returning to Flat after hurdles stint with concerning 605-day absence, prominent runner may struggle with race fitness despite going preference
runners_data.comment: Dual hurdles winner late last year; has winning form over this trip on the Flat
runners_data.spotlight: Two hurdle wins late last year and he's held his form pretty well in that discipline, last seen six weeks ago; his last Flat race was in 2024 for his former yard and peak form that year (1m6f win) suggests this is a realistic mark.

runners_data.name: Call My Bluff
runners_data.note: Prominent type who made all when winning at Newbury but disappointed here last year, veteran form hard to trust
runners_data.comment: Back to life at Newbury latest and has fine record here; returned to serious calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Won here in 2020 but last in this race last year; back to life at Newbury (2m, good; fine on soft) this April, making all in a six-runner race, but a sluggish start immediately put him on the back foot in the Chester Plate (10-1) one month ago and he ended up last of 17; well treated on old form but perhaps needs things to go his own way these days.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with solid recent course win but failed to fire in more competitive heat last time
runners_data.comment: Winning start for Henrietta Knight at Thirsk last month but this is a much stronger race
runners_data.spotlight: Had a 1m4f win for Mick Appleby last September and another for Henrietta Knight at Thirsk this April; however, no show in a more competitive race on latest start, has never won over further than 1m4f and, although probably stays 1m6f, his sole attempt at 2m (final start last term) was not persuasive.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: French soft ground winner adapting to British racing, prominent style suits but only one UK run to assess
runners_data.spotlight: Dual soft-ground winner (1m4f/2m) in France last autumn, from just four races there; picked up for 105,000euros in November and put up a bold show when fourth of 17 at York (1m4f, good) last month; stuck to his task at 20-1 that day and looks a strong candidate if that run has brought him on.

runners_data.name: Alfred Boucher
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse dropping down in grade after Salisbury win, proven stamina and tactical speed appeals
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced since 2022 but on a dangerous mark; watch the market on this return
runners_data.spotlight: Pipped in the 2022 Ebor; he's now a 10yo and very lightly raced in recent seasons but had sunk way down the weights before winning pretty smoothly at Salisbury (1m6f) last month on third start for this yard; bit to prove these days on softer than good; also back up 4lb but stays 2m and still thrown in judged on his old form.

runners_data.name: Maxident
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner returning after 271-day break but excellent soft ground record and course form compensates
runners_data.spotlight: Effective here; goes well on testing ground, as he showed again when winning at Ffos Las (1m6f; stays 2m+) in September on latest start; 3lb rise today is far less concerning than a move away from soft or heavy ground; big player if conditions are in his favour.

runners_data.name: Youthful King
runners_data.note: Hold-up type 6lb lower than last winning mark but poor recent form and claimer booking suggests limitations
runners_data.comment: 4lb below last winning mark, but has suffered heavy defeats in his last four starts
runners_data.spotlight: 6lb lower than when winning at Sandown (1m6f, good to firm) last June under Jack Dace, who frequently rides him; has not beaten many in his four starts this season, however; has one piece of form at this track (2022) but something to prove on softer than good.

runners_data.name: Russian Rumour
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up horse with recent wins but lacks course experience and 9yo consistency concerns
runners_data.comment: Course winner who bids a for hat-trick from a 2lb higher mark; much respected
runners_data.spotlight: 10-58 overall for this 9yo, with none of those races at this track; can make the running; won at Ffos Las (2m, heavy) last September (by 12l) and Nottingham (1m6f, good) this May; not far away when third of four at Lingfield 12 days ago in hat-trick bid and has an each-way chance.

runners_data.name: Arc Zoosve
runners_data.note: Non-runner but hold-up type in tremendous form with four straight wins in cheekpieces
runners_data.spotlight: Thriving since the cheekpieces went on in December, winning six of his nine starts in them; that includes his last four races and although the big majority of those runs were on AW, he also scored in a seven-runner race over C&D (good; made all) on penultimate outing; not proven on softer than good (well beaten on soft in October) but, after a comfortable AW win last time, he could still have more improvement in him.

races.paceDynamic: Maxident provides the only confirmed front-running presence and will likely dictate proceedings from the start, with Call My Bluff and Hermetic the most likely to press early if choosing to be positive. The lack of natural pace-pressers means Maxident can likely control the tempo without being harassed, creating a potentially steady gallop that builds gradually. Russian Rumour can also lead if connections choose, but the overall pace setup looks quite sedate given the long distance and testing ground. This tactical scenario strongly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and hold-up horses with a strong finishing kick, as they'll have first run on a potentially modest tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Maxident leads unopposed and sets a steady tempo through the first mile
scenarios.body: The genuine stayers get into a rhythm behind before the race develops into a sprint finish from the 3f pole. Patient hold-up horses with proven stamina get the best of the conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Call My Bluff or Russian Rumour decide to press Maxident early and create genuine pace
scenarios.body: The early tempo becomes more honest which suits the proven soft ground performers who can settle mid-division. Horses with tactical speed benefit from the stronger gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Maxident Dominates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Maxident gets completely uncontested lead and kicks clear from 4f out
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage before the field can respond on the testing ground. Front-running stamina prevails over finishing speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Crawling Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If the entire field goes to sleep through the middle stages with nobody willing to go forward
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from 3f out which suits horses with natural finishing speed regardless of stamina. The strongest finisher wins from an impossible position.

watchPoints.text: Maxident's fitness after 271-day layoff could see him stop quickly if the break tells in the final two furlongs
Call My Bluff's front-running tactics if he decides to press Maxident early and create uncharacteristic pace pressure
Alfred Boucher's ability to get a clear run from his hold-up position given the small field and potential bunching
Russian Rumour and In The Breeze both coming back quickly from recent runs within 12-29 days which could impact stamina
The claiming jockeys on Youthful King and Russian Rumour potentially getting outmaneuvered tactically in a slowly-run race

races.name: Tapster Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Hamish
runners_data.note: 10-year-old hold-up specialist with excellent course record who thrives on soft ground over this exact distance but hasn't raced for 225 days.
runners_data.spotlight: 10yo who's won a hatful of Group 3s at 1m4f-1m6f in his long and distinguished career, including at Newbury in October when last seen; has been kept to ground softer than good for a long time; kicked off that 2025 campaign with a win in this race and this star has good chance to repeat the dose.

runners_data.name: Glen Buck
runners_data.note: Limited experience 5-year-old making Listed debut after handicap success, with hold-up style suiting race shape but questions over this class level.
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who has had only six races, winning four; not discredited in April 2025 (1m2f; best form at 1m4f) when last seen but this graduation from handicaps seems a stiff task and it's also his turf debut.

runners_data.name: Arabian Crown
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter who gets dream scenario with uncontested lead but must prove stamina after 288-day layoff following disappointing 2024 campaign.
runners_data.spotlight: 2024 Sandown Classic Trial winner (good to soft) who missed the rest of that season; underwhelming on first four starts last year and ran particularly poorly at Glorious Goodwood (sole visit here) but he ended that campaign by winning narrowly in a four-runner Listed race at Windsor in August; needs to build on that but should stay 1m4f.

runners_data.name: Tenability
runners_data.note: Progressive 4-year-old closer with excellent Ascot 1m4f record and recent Group 3 form giving him clear class credentials for this contest.
runners_data.comment: Did well last term; his form is not what's required to win this but he brings potential
runners_data.spotlight: Won a novice and three Ascot 1m4f handicaps on varied ground last June-September; pipped a below-form Hamish for second in Ascot Group 3 on final outing last year and resumed his progress when he reappeared with a close third in Newbury Group 3 (1m4f, good) in April; that puts him into very serious contention today.

runners_data.name: Midak
runners_data.note: French-trained prominent runner whose Derby flop remains a concern but 1m4f soft ground experience could see improved performance in smaller field.
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first three races in France last year and started just 9-1 when brought over for the Derby but faded badly into tenth; ran respectably over 1m1f (soft) in October on his only subsequent start for Francis Graffard but an also-ran in the UAE this year over 1m1f (Group 1) and 1m2f (Listed) on both starts since 300,000euros sale in November; plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Involvement
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse showing career-best recent form at Goodwood with 16-day turnaround providing fitness edge over several longer-absent rivals.
runners_data.comment: Retains plenty of ability but has something to find back on home soil
runners_data.spotlight: Missed 2025; started this season at Meydan and Longchamp but returned to British soil with career-best form 16 days ago when a close fourth of nine in 1m2f Listed race at this track; more to prove on softer than good and this is also his first appearance beyond 1m2f, but that latest run gave some encouragement; either way he needs to find a bit extra.

races.paceDynamic: Arabian Crown is the only confirmed front runner in this 6-runner field and will face no early pressure, allowing him to dictate terms at a comfortable gallop over the extended 1m4f trip. Behind him, Midak may track prominently while the majority including Hamish, Tenability, Glen Buck and Involvement will settle towards the rear, creating a bunched field turning for home. With soft ground testing stamina reserves and one uncontested leader controlling the tempo, this race sets up perfectly for hold-up horses who can finish strongly. The tactical advantage clearly favours the closers who can unleash late runs behind what should be an honest but sustainable pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown sets honest fractions without pressure and the hold-up brigade gets the perfect setup
scenarios.body: The soft ground aids stamina while multiple closers get first run on the tiring leader, with class horses like Hamish and Tenability thriving in these conditions. This becomes a cavalry charge from the back with the best stayers prevailing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown's uncontested lead proves too valuable and he finds enough reserves in the closing stages
scenarios.body: The 3-year-old's previous Listed success at Goodwood gives him course knowledge while his proven 1m4f ability shines through when not harassed early. The closers leave their run too late on testing ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow early and horses positioned just behind the leader get first run
scenarios.body: Midak's prominent position allows him to strike before the back markers can respond, while the soft ground suits his staying pedigree. The hold-up horses are caught flat-footed by the sudden injection of pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Arabian Crown sets crawling fractions and the race becomes a sprint finish rather than a staying test
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace turns this into a muddling affair where tactical speed matters more than stamina, catching the proven stayers cold. Fresh legs and tactical positioning become crucial in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Arabian Crown goes too fast early - his previous tendency to race keenly could see him empty out despite having the lead to himself.
Monitor Hamish's jumping from the gates after his long absence - any slow start would be fatal for a hold-up horse in this small field.
Keep an eye on Midak's early positioning with Jamie Spencer aboard - his prominent style could be crucial if the pace becomes pedestrian.
Watch for Glen Buck's inexperience at this level showing when the pace quickens - stepping up from handicaps to Listed company is a significant jump.
Observe how Tenability travels through the race given his quick reappearance - any signs of laboring could indicate the 50-day break wasn't sufficient.

races.name: Elston Support Your Local Air Ambulance Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamondonthehill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should get soft lead but has been hard to win with lately despite consistent efforts
runners_data.comment: Solid AW campaign this winter but he wasn't at his best returned to turf 12 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Capable of useful form but not easy to win with these days, getting little respite from the handicapper; another solid effort when second at Musselburgh 17 days ago (7f, good) but others appeal more for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Cherry Cobbler
runners_data.note: Pace-setting type coming off impressive Newmarket win but faces 8lb rise and switch from good to soft ground
runners_data.comment: Down in the weights but form has gone wrong way since his promising handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on his reduced mark when running away with a 7f handicap at Newmarket three weeks ago (good ground); hit with an 8lb rise but he has had few chances at the trip; untested on slower than good.

runners_data.name: Dr Strangelove
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse back to last winning mark, effective at 7f but faces traffic problems with so many similar types
runners_data.spotlight: His two wins have come over 6f but he is fully effective over this extra furlong; back to his last winning mark and he will be a danger to all if the ground is suitable (well beaten in one run on slower than good).

runners_data.name: Blue Prince
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with strong course form whose reappearance third suggests return to form but needs luck in running
runners_data.comment: Non-runner
runners_data.spotlight: Has some strong C&D form; the second half of 2025 was disappointing but he dropped in the weights and his reappearance third at Kempton was a welcome return to form; big player.

runners_data.name: Wobwobwob
runners_data.note: Prominent type on long losing run but soft ground could spark interest after two years without success
runners_data.comment: Retains a good chunk of ability but the drying ground will compromise his chance today
runners_data.spotlight: Losing run stretches back over two years and neither start this year suggests he is ready to exploit his lowly mark; the prospect of slow ground does pique interest though.

runners_data.name: Rare Change
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course form from successful spell last year but inconsistent since and needs clear passage
runners_data.comment: Good spell around this time last year; possibilities if taking well to refitted blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Had bad luck in running over C&D during an otherwise successful spell around this time last year; inconsistent since but has possibilities off current mark with cheekpieces given another spin.

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner building on recent Lingfield win but faces significant class rise and 7lb penalty against better horses
runners_data.comment: Won twice last term but below that form this year.
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on the drop to Class 6 company when running away with a Lingfield handicap (7f, good) 19 days ago; the 7lb rise against stiffer opposition should find her out.

runners_data.name: Serenity Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who won here last year off lower mark but looks outgunned by stronger opposition despite decent recent form
runners_data.comment: Chance on this winter's AW best but he was well beaten back on turf last week
runners_data.spotlight: Win here last August (6f) came off 2lb lower; several good runs this year, including in a big field at Ascot four weeks ago, but others look stronger for win purposes.

runners_data.name: Dannick
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden without impact in two runs this year following wind operation, cheekpieces addition unlikely to transform
runners_data.comment: 13-race maiden who returned after wind surgery with a laboured effort over C&D 16 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: 14-race maiden; no impact in his two runs this year (following a wind operation) and the addition of cheekpieces isn't enough to tempt.

races.paceDynamic: Diamondonthehill and Cherry Cobbler will set a controlled pace from the front, with Wobwobwob likely to press from prominent position early. The soft ground combined with 7f at Goodwood should create a steady but not punishing tempo through the first 4f. With six hold-up horses including Dr Strangelove, Blue Prince and Rare Change all looking to come with late runs, this sets up perfectly for the prominent racers to steal a march. The tactical verdict strongly favours prominent/pace-setting horses who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large hold-up contingent on soft ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Diamondonthehill and Cherry Cobbler maintain control without excessive pressure
scenarios.body: The pace-setters get first run on the field while hold-up horses struggle for racing room and kick on testing ground. Prominent runners exploit their positional advantage as the large pack of hold-up horses gets shuffled back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late surge succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes overly strong or prominent horses tie up
scenarios.body: The soft ground finds out the early leaders in the final furlong, allowing the stronger stayers to pick up the pieces. Dr Strangelove and Blue Prince benefit from their hold-up style as others come back to them.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Improving handicapper strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido's recent Lingfield win translates to this higher grade
scenarios.body: His momentum from that dominant Class 6 victory carries him through despite the 7lb rise and tougher opposition. The soft ground suits his style and he finds gaps that others cannot.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If no horse wants the early lead and they crawl through splits
scenarios.body: An extremely tactical affair becomes a sprint from 2f out, suiting horses with the best turn of foot regardless of position. Raw ability trumps tactics in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Cherry Cobbler could prove too strong if handling the soft ground switch after his impressive Newmarket success on good
Dr Strangelove will need significant luck in running with six other hold-up horses creating inevitable traffic problems
Tronido's confidence from recent Lingfield romp could carry him beyond his apparent class ceiling
Wobwobwob might finally end losing streak if soft ground rekindles old enthusiasm but form suggests otherwise
Diamondonthehill should get uncontested lead but recent seconds suggest he may lack winning punch despite good position
